title: Weyl group of E8
description: W(E8) is the finite reflection group generated by the 240 root reflections of the E8 root system. It is the automorphism group of the root system that preserves the Euclidean form. Order 696729600. Elements are isometries: for w in W(E8), w inverse equals the adjoint of w. This does not make an arbitrary matrix into a Weyl element.
definitions: A simple reflection s_alpha sends x to x - 2 <x,alpha>/<alpha,alpha> alpha.
W(E8) is generated by eight simple reflections of the E8 Dynkin diagram.
The Coxeter element is the product of the eight simple reflections (any order of a Coxeter word).
equations: s_alpha(x) = x - <x,alpha> alpha  for roots of norm 2
w^{-1} = w*  for every w in W(E8)
assumptions: The 240 roots are the norm-2 lattice vectors of L_E8.
mechanism: Reflections in root hyperplanes generate a finite subgroup of O(8). That subgroup is the symmetry that actually inverts: only its own elements.
falsification_conditions: A reflection in a non-root hyperplane that still preserves the root system.
confusion_guard: w inverse = w* holds inside W(E8). It does not hold for a Moore-Penrose inverse of an unnamed map into R^8. Self-duality of the lattice is a different statement.
primary_sources: Humphreys, Reflection Groups and Coxeter Groups
Bourbaki, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Ch. VI
predictions: Every w in W(E8) permutes the 240 roots.
